newsitem.title: INDIA: India bus bomb kills one, injures 19.
newsitem.headline: India bus bomb kills one, injures 19.

text.p: A blast ripped through a privately-owned bus in the northern Indian town of Panipat on Saturday, killing one person and injuring at least 19 people, police and hospital officials said.
They said the blast occurred at 4.55 p.m. (1125 GMT) as the bus was parked in the main bus station of the town, some 100 km (60 miles) north of New Delhi in Haryana state.
"So far one person has died, a boy," D.P.Arora, a doctor at Panipat's civil hospital, told Reuters by telephone.
He said at least 19 people were injured, and added that he did not expect any more deaths.
"It was a crude bomb, not an RDX (research developed explosive) bomb," said an aide of the district chief, quoting a senior police official.

"The blast took place as the bus stopped and people were getting down," Rajpal Khurana, conductor of a state-run bus service in Haryana, who was present at the site of the blast, told Reuters by telephone from the bus station.

"We carried away the injured people to hospital in scooter rickshaws," said Khurana. "Three of the people appeared serious. They were covered with blood and in some cases the bones were visible. It seemed as if their legs had been severely damaged."
"This is the third explosion in the area and looks like some (organised) group is involved," F.C.Kansal, Haryana's police chief, told Reuters at Chandigarh, the state capital.
Bomb blasts in northern India are usually blamed on suspected Kashmiri or Sikh separatists.
On January 21, police in Delhi seized five kg (11 lb) of RDX from a raid on a city hotel and arrested three suspected Kashmiri separatist militants.

The raid came ahead of the Republic Day, January 26. Officials said separatists planned blasts ahead of the anniversary of the day, when India celebrates the adoption of its republican constitution in 1950.

On January 4, two bombs, one in a bus and the other in a taxi, exploded minutes apart in the Indian capital killing one person and injuring 11. The bus was on its way from Delhi to Sonepat, located on the highway that connects to Panipat.
At least 31 people were killed in three separate bomb attacks in the capital over the past year.
